title: unramified omega zero
conclusions: f unramified iff f locally finite type and Ω_{X/S}=0
f G-unramified iff f locally finite presentation and Ω_{X/S}=0
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is unramified if and only if $f$ is locally of finite type
and $\Omega_{X/S} = 0$, and
\item $f$ is G-unramified if and only if $f$ is locally of finite presentation
and $\Omega_{X/S} = 0$.
\end{enumerate}

title: unramified characterize
conclusions: If these hold, arbitrary compatible restrictions U→V preserve same respective unramifiedness
equivalent_conditions: For all compatible affine U,V, ring map O_S(V)→O_X(U) unramified (resp. G-unramified)
Exist ordinary covers V_j,U_i with all U_i→V_j unramified (resp. G-unramified)
Exist affine covers with induced rings maps unramified (resp. G-unramified)
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified).
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$
with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map
$\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified).
\item There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$
is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified).
\item There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is
unramified (resp.\ G-unramified), for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $f$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified) then for
any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$
the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified).

title: composition unramified
explicit_hypotheses: Composites X→Y→Z of schemes, both maps unramified (respectively G-unramified)
conclusions: Composite unramified (respectively G-unramified)
standalone_statement_latex: For composable morphisms of schemes \(X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z\), the composite is unramified when both morphisms are unramified, and is G-unramified when both are G-unramified.

title: base change unramified
conclusions: Base change X×_S S'→S' is unramified (respectively G-unramified)
standalone_statement_latex: For any morphism of schemes \(S'\to S\), base change preserves unramified morphisms of schemes and also preserves G-unramified morphisms of schemes.

title: noetherian unramified
conclusions: f unramified iff f G-unramified
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ is locally Noetherian.
Then $f$ is unramified if and only if $f$ is G-unramified.

title: open immersion unramified
conclusions: j G-unramified
standalone_statement_latex: Every open immersion \(j:U\hookrightarrow X\) of schemes is G-unramified.

title: closed immersion unramified
conclusions: i is unramified
i is G-unramified iff I finite type as O_X-module
standalone_statement_latex:
A closed immersion $i : Z \to X$ is unramified.
It is G-unramified if and only if the associated quasi-coherent sheaf of
ideals $\mathcal{I} = \Ker(\mathcal{O}_X \to i_*\mathcal{O}_Z)$
is of finite type (as an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module).

title: unramified locally finite type
conclusions: f unramified implies f locally finite type
f G-unramified implies f locally finite presentation
standalone_statement_latex: If \(f:X\to S\) is an unramified morphism of schemes, then \(f\) is locally of finite type. If \(f\) is G-unramified, then \(f\) is locally of finite presentation.

title: unramified quasi finite
conclusions: f quasi-finite at x
Consequently globally unramified morphisms are locally quasi-finite
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to S\) be a morphism of schemes and \(x\in X\). If \(f\) is unramified at \(x\), then it is quasi-finite at \(x\). In particular, if \(f\) is unramified everywhere, then \(f\) is locally quasi-finite.

title: unramified etale fibres
conclusions: If f unramified, κ(x)/κ(f(x)) finite separable for every x
If f locally finite type and all scheme fibres disjoint unions of spectra of finite separable field extensions, f unramified
If f locally finite presentation and all scheme fibres have that description, f G-unramified
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f$ is unramified then for any $x \in X$ the field extension
$\kappa(x)/\kappa(f(x))$ is finite separable.
\item If $f$ is locally of finite type, and for every
$s \in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable
field extensions of $\kappa(s)$ then $f$ is unramified.
\item If $f$ is locally of finite presentation, and for every
$s \in S$ the fibre $X_s$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable
field extensions of $\kappa(s)$ then $f$ is G-unramified.
\end{enumerate}

title: diagonal unramified morphism
conclusions: If f unramified then Δ_f open immersion
If Δ_f open immersion and f locally finite type then f unramified
If Δ_f open immersion and f locally finite presentation then f G-unramified
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f$ is unramified, then the diagonal morphism
$\Delta : X \to X \times_S X$ is an open immersion.
\item If $f$ is locally of finite type
and $\Delta$ is an open immersion, then $f$ is unramified.
\item If $f$ is locally of finite presentation and $\Delta$ is an open
immersion, then $f$ is G-unramified.
\end{enumerate}

title: unramified at point
explicit_hypotheses: f locally finite type for unramified version, respectively locally finite presentation for G-unramified version
equivalent_conditions: Fibre X_s unramified over κ(s) at x
Differentials after tensoring with κ(x) vanish
m_s O_{X,x}=m_x and κ(x)/κ(s) finite separable
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $x \in X$.
Set $s = f(x)$.
Assume $f$ is locally of finite type (resp.\ locally of finite presentation).
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is unramified (resp.\ G-unramified) at $x$.
\item The fibre $X_s$ is unramified over $\kappa(s)$ at $x$.
\item The $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-module $\Omega_{X/S, x}$ is zero.
\item The $\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}$-module $\Omega_{X_s/s, x}$ is zero.
\item The $\kappa(x)$-vector space
$$
\Omega_{X_s/s, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X_s, x}} \kappa(x) =
\Omega_{X/S, x} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x}} \kappa(x)
$$
is zero.
\item We have $\mathfrak m_s\mathcal{O}_{X, x} = \mathfrak m_x$
and the field extension $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is finite
separable.
\end{enumerate}

title: set points where fibres unramified
explicit_hypotheses: T={x∈X: fibre X_{f(x)} unramified over κ(f(x)) at x}
S'→S arbitrary and X'=X×_S S', projection g':X'→X
conclusions: T open and equals locus where f unramified
Corresponding base-change T'=(g')^{-1}(T)
If f locally finite presentation, analogous openness/base change for G-unramified locus
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Assume $f$ locally of finite type. Formation of the open set
\begin{align*}
T
& =
\{x \in X \mid X_{f(x)}\text{ is unramified over }\kappa(f(x))\text{ at }x\} \\
& =
\{x \in X \mid X\text{ is unramified over }S\text{ at }x\}
\end{align*}
commutes with arbitrary base change:
For any morphism $g : S' \to S$, consider
the base change $f' : X' \to S'$ of $f$ and the
projection $g' : X' \to X$. Then the corresponding
set $T'$ for the morphism $f'$ is equal to $T' = (g')^{-1}(T)$.
If $f$ is assumed locally of finite presentation then the same holds
for the open set of points where $f$ is G-unramified.

title: unramified permanence
explicit_hypotheses: f:X→Y morphism of schemes over S
conclusions: If X→S unramified then X→Y unramified
If X→S G-unramified and Y→S locally finite type then X→Y G-unramified

title: value at one point
explicit_hypotheses: Residue field maps κ(y)→κ(x) from f and g coincide
conclusions: There is open neighborhood U of x on which f|_U=g|_U
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$, $Y$ be schemes over $S$.
Let $f, g : X \to Y$ be morphisms over $S$. Let $x \in X$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the structure morphism $Y \to S$ is unramified,
\item $f(x) = g(x)$ in $Y$, say $y = f(x) = g(x)$, and
\item the induced maps $f^\sharp, g^\sharp : \kappa(y) \to \kappa(x)$
are equal.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an open neighbourhood of $x$ in $X$ on which
$f$ and $g$ are equal.
